title: Lincoln in the Bardo
author: George Saunders
summary: In 1862, a president's young son dies and is laid to rest in a Washington cemetery. His spirit lingers among the other ghosts, a chorus of voices that tries to coax him onward.
readIf: you want an inventive, quick-moving book made of many voices, and do not mind being moved.
skipIf: you prefer conventional narration; it reads like a script with quoted fragments and ghostly overlapping speakers.

pairings.reason: Another novel that gives the dead a voice and treats grief as something both sad and strangely hopeful.
A war-time story narrated by Death that also looks at loss from an unexpected angle.
Likewise mixes history, tragedy and surreal elements in a short, formally playful book.
